name: Monthly port reports its outcome and writes the metrics file
non_visual_rationale: A monthly JSON for Andres with no reader at launch has no pixels to check; the operator reads it directly, which is what the steps do.
criteria_delivered: 1. runMonthlyEvaluationOnce({ store, clock, spots? }) returns { completed, verdict, metrics_key, events }, never a bare void -- proven by the acceptance test's own port-absence-then-outcome assertions.

2. One metrics file lands under learned/metrics/v1/dt=<YYYY-MM>/metrics.json, the month taken from the injected clock (never the wall clock), holding all six named sections: selection, pairwise, mae, sigma_human, calibration, shrinkage, cv.

3. selection carries per_decile (decile, calls, reported_days) and solicited_share; pairwise carries pairs and target_pairs: 400; mae carries per_key entries plus baselines.climatology and baselines.persistence, both computed honestly from the observation log rather than shipped as null literals.
4. The file is operator-facing only: nothing under src/ or tests/ reads learned/metrics/v1/ except the acceptance harness itself.

5. D-2026-08-12-1's ruling holds: the run writes exactly one key, under learned/metrics/v1/, and the harness's full-store snapshot diff (assertWritesConfinedToMetrics) finds no other byte created, rewritten or deleted. The ruled-out mechanism (recover/learning-build's evaluate.ts:36-38, an in-place rewrite of learned/corrections/v1/current/ on a kill verdict) was read for reference and not ported in any form -- this module reads that prefix (for the shrinkage section) but never writes to it, and a dedicated unit test drives the real port against a real in-memory store holding a correction file, proving the read path is exercised rather than bypassed.
criteria_deferred: cv.verdict's actual judgment: the rolling-origin held-out CV comparing corrected vs raw MAE (06 section 7 G7) is 05-02's. This step ships the literal 'not_evaluated' honestly -- zero applied correction keys exist at launch, and reporting an unbuilt judgment as anything else would claim certainty the code does not earn.
calibration.offending_term naming which confidence term failed the check (09 section 3.6, section 10.2) is 05-04's. This step ships the bins the naming logic will read and the literal null.

shrinkage[].flagged, the >=80-observations/>=60%-shrunk alarm (09 section 17.4 guardrail 2), is 05-05's. This step ships every gated spot's row read honestly off its stored correction (shrink_weight, n, reporters) with the literal false.
scope_note: support/monthly-port.ts's dynamic import was left untouched: the RED run (files moved aside, see red_evidence) proved the const-string import already reports port-absence correctly under vitest/node, so the documented literal-string trap did not fire and no edit to shared test infrastructure was needed. Two rounds of self-review before commit (this lane's own, plus one advisor pass) caught defects worth naming rather than quietly fixing: (a) the first cut of mae.per_key keyed only on (source, leadBucket), which would silently average two spots' errors into one number the moment they shared a source and lead bucket -- fixed by looping spotsReportedIn(observations) and filtering per spot before calling formHeightResidualRows, matching fit.ts's own precedent, and verified with a throwaway two-spot script showing two distinct rows post-fix; (b) the mae.per_key map key was for a time joined with a plain space, which is not collision-safe against permissively-parsed spot_id/source strings that could themselves contain a space -- switched to a double-colon join, documented in the code as a display-safe low-collision choice rather than an unrepresentable-character guarantee; (c) the second advisor pass found that all eight original unit tests drove buildMonthlyMetrics directly, so evaluate.ts's own readCurrentCorrections (the store list/get calls and parseStoredCorrection's refusal branches) had no test requiring it -- closed with two more tests driving the real runMonthlyEvaluationOnce port against a real InMemoryStore, one discriminating test verified by stubbing readCurrentCorrections to return [] and watching it fail for the right reason before being reverted.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: mae.per_key is keyed on (spot_id, source, lead_bucket), not (source, lead_bucket) alone. 06 section 10's table says 'per key' without spelling out that a key spans spots; HeightResidualRow itself is spot-blind by residuals.ts's own design (the caller states the spot). This module states it the same way fit.ts does: filter observations to one spot before forming residual rows, so two spots sharing a source and lead bucket never collapse into one averaged number. 06 section 2's consumer table gives the join key as (month, spot_id), which this key shape now actually supports. The map key's own three parts join on a double colon rather than a space, because spot_id and source both come off permissively-parsed log rows and either could legally contain a space; a double colon is a display-safe low-collision choice, not a security boundary.

mae.baselines and mae.per_key are computed over sample sets that are honest but not identical. per_key only covers observations that PAIRED with a prediction (formHeightResidualRows' own pairing rule); baselines.climatology and baselines.persistence cover every observation with a readable size_band and day, paired or not, because a climatology or persistence baseline needs no forecast to compare against. 'Did the model beat climatology' is therefore not an apples-to-apples subtraction of the two numbers in this file without also checking each side's own n -- flagged here rather than silently reconciled, since reconciling would mean inventing a forecast for an unpaired report.

baselines.climatology and baselines.persistence are null when no data supports them (zero readable points, or no yesterday), and this module never falls back to 06 section 4's S4 default of 0.5 m. That default is stated for C_track's publication-time computation, a different consumer with a different honesty contract (it must always print SOME number); this operator file's contract is the opposite -- say so when a number cannot be earned, per the repo's own rule against claiming more certainty than the data holds.

calibration reads predicted.conf_level through a local, module-private type view (CapturedPredictedBlock) rather than widening ObservationRow['predicted'] in src/learning/inputs.ts. The shared type stays { score_q: number } | null as every other consumer of it expects; a row missing conf_level (or carrying a non-string) is simply excluded from every confidence bin, the same permissive-read stance inputs.ts already takes on every other optional field.

pairwise's 'same local day' is read as the UTC calendar day of observed_at. No timezone carrier exists on ObservationRow today, so this is the honest reading of what the log actually stores rather than an invented Panama-local offset; the same reading pairwise-groups by (reporter_key, day) using reporterKeyOf, the already-exported C5 resolution residuals.ts uses for exactly this purpose.

The port signature carries an optional spots?: readonly unknown[] parameter for parity with runLearningFitOnce's own LearningFitDeps.spots? seam (criterion 1's documented shape). It is accepted and unused this step -- no pooling decision runs inside a metrics-only job -- so that a later step needing the seed roster widens this same parameter instead of adding a second one.
acceptance: tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/the-monthly-file-watches-every-hazard-the-design-names.test.ts, one scenario over the real runMonthlyEvaluationOnce port via the shared driveMonthlyEvaluationOnce harness (dynamic-import by design, so a not-yet-scaffolded port fails at an assertion rather than a collection error). A month of 30 mornings at playa-venao (alternating good/ok quality, one in three flagged push_solicited) plus 90 days of published calls cycling every score decile. Asserts: outcome.completed, outcome.verdict in the three-value vocabulary, outcome.events is an array, assertWritesConfinedToMetrics reports exactly one new key (the clock's own dt=2026-08 metrics file, never the wall-clock date), outcome.metrics_key names that same key, and every 06 section 10 field the design names is present with the right shape (selection.per_decile rows, selection.solicited_share, pairwise.pairs/target_pairs, mae.baselines.{climatology,persistence}, sigma_human.co_observer_pairs, calibration, shrinkage array, cv.verdict).
unit_law: Ten fast-check properties/examples in tests/unit/learning-metrics.test.ts, eight against buildMonthlyMetrics (the pure builder's own driving port) and two against runMonthlyEvaluationOnce (the real store-reading port), covering branches the single-spot, zero-correction AT fixture cannot reach: (1) selection.solicited_share stays inside [0,1] for any generated log; (2-3) pairwise excludes a same-reporter same-day pair whose quality labels tie and excludes a same-spot pair entirely, whatever the labels; (4) sigma_human's co-observer count and disagreement value do not depend on report order and are never negative; (5) mae.baselines.climatology is exactly zero and .persistence is exactly null for one isolated report, for any spot and band; (6) mae.per_key matches an independently computed |hEff(swell_h_m, swell_t_s) - mid(band)| oracle for one exactly-paired report (Hebert's Modeling strategy -- this is the test that would have caught the per-key spot-collapse bug named in scope_note, had it not already been self-caught); (7-8) buildMonthlyMetrics's shrinkage reads shrink_weight/n/reporters straight off a stored correction's fullest applied key, and reports nothing for a correction whose only key was gate-refused; (9-10) runMonthlyEvaluationOnce reads a real correction file with two applied keys off a real InMemoryStore and writes the fullest one's fields into the metrics file it names in its own outcome, and reads an unparseable correction byte as absent rather than crashing the run. (9) was verified discriminating: stubbing readCurrentCorrections to return [] unconditionally made it fail for the right reason before the stub was reverted.
test_budget: Behaviours: (1) solicited_share bound, (2) pairwise cross-spot requirement, (3) pairwise tie-exclusion, (4) sigma_human order-independence/non-negativity, (5) mae baselines on a degenerate fixture, (6) mae.per_key against an independent oracle, (7) shrinkage reads a gated spot's own fields (builder), (8) shrinkage omits an ungated spot (builder), (9) the real port reads corrections off the real store and reports the fullest applied key, (10) the real port reads an unparseable correction byte as absent. Ten behaviours, budget 20. Delivered 10: one property or example test per behaviour, none parametrize-inflated (nw-test-optimization skill section 4 procedure run).
red_evidence: The pre-authored AT was unskipped, then src/learning/evaluate.ts and src/learning/metrics.ts were moved out of the tree (not merely reverted with git, since they were untracked) and the AT re-run: 1 test collected, 1 failed, semantic AssertionError -- 'the monthly evaluation port does not exist yet: nothing at src/learning/evaluate.ts answers when the monthly conscience is asked to run (accepted roadmap 05-01)' -- no collection or import errors. The two files were then moved back before any GREEN work proceeded.
falsifiability_evidence: Two controlled mutations, each reverted and re-verified. (1) METRICS_PREFIX in src/learning/evaluate.ts changed from 'learned/metrics/v1/' to 'learned/wrong-prefix/v1/': AT failed with AssertionError 'the monthly evaluation CREATED learned/wrong-prefix/v1/dt=2026-08/metrics.json: a metrics-only job writes under learned/metrics/v1/ and nowhere else (D-2026-08-12-1)', from assertWritesConfinedToMetrics -- exactly the ruling this step exists to enforce. (2) readCurrentCorrections stubbed to return [] unconditionally: the new corrections-read unit test failed with a deepEqual mismatch expecting the n=50 shrinkage row and receiving []. Both reverted; diff against a pre-mutation copy showed zero bytes different each time; both suites re-run green.
gates_run: npm run typecheck: exit 0. Full suite (npx vitest run, no filter): 106 files, 97 passed / 4 failed (5 individual tests) / 5 skipped; 532 tests, 520 passed / 5 failed / 7 skipped. The 5 failures are exactly the pre-existing, HANDOFF-documented family named in this step's own task context (tests/unit/staleness-stamp.test.ts, staleness-stamp-format.test.ts, staleness-flip.test.ts, report-island.test.ts -- the civil-day build refusal) and are unchanged in count and identity from the run taken before this step's files existed. git status --porcelain confirms only this step's owned paths are touched.
known_flake: Unchanged from prior steps: npm run build is refused by the civil-day check in src/publish/publish-static-surface.ts once Panama's local date has rolled past data/published-surface.json's published day, and the 5 staleness/report-island unit failures above trace to the same clock-vs-fixture gap. Neither is this lane's; this step performs no UI-affecting change and did not run npm run build.
